audit.evidence: Live gate on real Docker: real npm netmask package bytes via npm aliases (netmask@1.0.6/2.0.0/2.0.1). original 0177.0.0.1 reaches flag@v0, blocked@v1; bypass 0X7f.0.0.1 reaches flag@v1 (residual); residual blocked@v2. passed=true, residual_blocked_on_v2=true via GET /fetch?host= HTTP trigger.

app_purpose: Node.js IPv4 block utility used as an SSRF / IP-ACL allow-deny guard (Netmask(block).contains(host))
root_cause: SSRF / IP-ACL bypass via IPv4 octal / edge-character parsing (CWE-918)

v0.ref: npm netmask@1.0.6 lib/netmask.js ip2long (ignores leading zeros; octal 0177 misread as decimal 177)

v1.ref: npm netmask@2.0.0 lib/netmask.js ip2long (CVE-2021-28918 fix: leading-0 octet parsed as octal; INCOMPLETE — hex test `byte[1]==='x' || byte[1]==='x'` typo mishandles uppercase 0X)

v2.ref: npm netmask@2.0.1 lib/netmask.js ip2long/atob (CVE-2021-29418 complete fix: strict char scanner handling 0x/0X and rejecting stray chars)

flag.resource: internal loopback sidecar (127.0.0.1:80, no host port) reachable only via the guarded fetch sink
flag.placement: harness.mjs runs a flag server bound to 127.0.0.1:80 inside each version's container serving ${PCB_FLAG}
flag.detect: flag token substring in candidate result body

evidence.fix_reference: npm netmask@2.0.0 lib/netmask.js ip2long (CVE-2021-28918 fix: leading-0 octet parsed as octal; INCOMPLETE — hex test `byte[1]==='x' || byte[1]==='x'` typo mishandles uppercase 0X); npm netmask@2.0.1 lib/netmask.js ip2long/atob (CVE-2021-29418 complete fix: strict char scanner handling 0x/0X and rejecting stray chars)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: netmask before 2.0.1 mishandles certain unexpected characters in an IP address string, such as an octal digit of 9 ... allows attackers to bypass access control based on IP addresses. This issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2021-28918.

provenance.notes: Faithful-core harness: the REAL npm `netmask` package installed per-version via npm aliases (netmask@1.0.6=V0, netmask@2.0.0=V1, netmask@2.0.1=V2). Guard = block iff any of {127/8,10/8,172.16/12,192.168/16,169.254/16} contains the RAW ?host= string (0.0.0.0/8 intentionally omitted — a common real-world denylist gap the residual exploits, since netmask 2.0.0 collapses the mishandled uppercase-hex octet to 0). Host read raw from the query param (no new URL / no legacy url.parse, which would canonicalise/lower-case the encoding). Node native fetch (undici) = outbound sink; loopback flag sidecar = canary (both crafted forms route to 127.0.0.1). Variant A gate passes; V2 negative control confirms the 2.0.1 complete fix. Gate run via `python3 oracle.py --wait`; see repro.log.
